notable_absence.finding: cbbackupmgr-config.md documents every --encrypted/--km-*/--passphrase flag in full but never once states that repository encryption is an Enterprise Edition feature - that fact only appears on the separate cbbackupmgr-encryption.md tutorial page ('A tutorial that explains how to use the encryption feature of cbbackupmgr Enterprise Edition.'). A reader who only consults the flag reference (this page) has no way to learn the feature is edition-gated at all.

cross_component_finding: config.md's --enable-users section requires exactly the three-way 8.0 role split the registry's role:ro-admin collision note already describes (Local User Security Admin / External User Security Admin / Read-Only Admin) plus Full Admin, but applied to a completely different surface than security pages: which USERS get included in a cbbackupmgr backup depends on which of these roles the operating user holds. This is independent confirmation, from a tooling reference page rather than a security page, that the 8.0 split is a real, consistently-applied product decision - and it forced minting role:external-user-security-administrator, which previously existed only as prose inside another concept's note, never as its own id.
cross_product_finding: The --capella flag ('Modifies the repository configuration to disable backing up the services that are not supported with Capella including: analytics, cluster analytics, bucket query, cluster query, views and users') shows that cbbackupmgr - a Server-only CLI with no Capella twin - can nonetheless produce a backup repository explicitly shaped for eventual use against a Capella cluster. This nuances the module's 'no Capella twin' framing: Capella does not expose cbbackupmgr, but cbbackupmgr is aware of Capella as a restore target and knows which services Capella doesn't support. Filed as a finding rather than a merge - no page states that a cbbackupmgr archive can actually be restored into Capella, only that the config command can be shaped for it.
